name: Multiple Mitochondrial DNA Deletion Syndrome
aliases: Progressive External Ophthalmoplegia with Multiple mtDNA Deletions
Mitochondrial DNA Depletion Syndrome with Multiple Deletions

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Multiple Mitochondrial DNA Deletion Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of progressive external ophthalmoplegia and/or skeletal myopathy
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-deficient fibers
Detection of multiple mitochondrial DNA deletions in muscle tissue or blood
Family history suggestive of mitochondrial inheritance or autosomal recessive pattern
Elevated serum lactate levels at rest or after exercise

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical features (progressive external ophthalmoplegia and/or myopathy), muscle biopsy findings, and genetic confirmation of multiple mtDNA deletions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, histopathological, and molecular genetic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Bilateral, symmetric limitation of eye movements

searchTerms: muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
abnormal muscle fibers with red staining
endocrine problems including blood sugar issues

laboratory: Abnormal oxidative phosphorylation enzyme activities in muscle
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle atrophy and fatty infiltration
Brain MRI may be normal or show mild nonspecific changes
genetic: Multiple mitochondrial DNA deletions detected by Southern blot or long-range PCR
Mutations in nuclear genes involved in mtDNA maintenance (e.g. POLG, TWNK)
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating ragged-red fibers and COX-deficient fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Single large-scale mtDNA deletion rather than multiple deletions
Phenotypes such as Kearns-Sayre syndrome with earlier onset
More prominent multisystem involvement including cardiac conduction defects and pigmentary retinopathy
POLG mutations may cause overlapping but broader phenotypes
May present with epilepsy, ataxia, and sensory neuropathy
More frequent liver involvement and earlier onset in some cases

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia with proximal muscle weakness
Elevated serum lactate at rest or after minimal exertion
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and multiple mtDNA deletions
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial DNA deletion syndromes. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
